note: 45 new practitioner entries extracted from the April 2026 seed taxonomy 'Digital Art Is the Art of Our Age' plus two adjacencies: Ben Fry (named in article), Golan Levin (from living graph spec), Jesse Kanda (named in article). Status: draft. Voice drawn from gatherer.md — declare bias, name what each practitioner foregrounds. Facts are conservative; where uncertain, 'uncertain: true'.

entries.name: Vera Molnár
entries.medium: algorithmic drawing, plotter art, computer graphics, systematic geometry
entries.summary: Pioneer of algorithmic art who began making systematic plotter drawings in 1968, before the field had a name. Her work explores disorder inside rigorous geometric constraint — the rule and the exception both visible in the same frame.

key_works.title: Interruptions
key_works.description: Plotter series disrupting a square grid with selective deletions — an early demonstration of variation as subject matter.

key_works.title: (Dés)Ordres
key_works.description: Algorithmic composition where ordered lines are gradually rotated out of register, making disorder a measurable quantity.

entries.name: Frieder Nake
entries.medium: plotter drawing, algorithmic art, computer graphics
entries.summary: Mathematician and artist who publicly exhibited computer-generated art in 1965, among the first three people in the world to do so. Also wrote the theoretical scaffolding the field would need before most people knew a field existed.

key_works.title: Hommage à Paul Klee 13/9/65 Nr.2
key_works.description: Plotter drawing on a Zuse Graphomat — one of the earliest publicly exhibited computer artworks.

entries.name: Manfred Mohr
entries.medium: algorithmic art, plotter drawing, hypercube geometry
entries.summary: Translates multidimensional geometry into visual form through algorithms. Got computer art into gallery walls when institutional resistance was near-total. His decades-long hypercube investigation is a single sustained argument.

key_works.title: P-159
key_works.description: Early cubic transformation series applying algorithmic deformation to the cube.

key_works.title: Dimensions
key_works.description: Long-running series projecting the hypercube into two dimensions through rotation and selection rules.

entries.name: Charles Csuri
entries.medium: plotter drawing, computer animation, digital art
entries.summary: Made computer-generated drawings and animations in the 1960s that now sit in the collections that define canons. Founded ACCAD at Ohio State — a bridge between art and computer science built when neither side recognized the other.

key_works.title: Hummingbird
key_works.description: Algorithmic transformation of a hand-drawn hummingbird, among the earliest recognized computer artworks.

entries.name: JODI
entries.medium: net art, browser-based art, software art
entries.summary: Joan Heemskerk and Dirk Paesmans broke the browser open. Cascading green text, deconstructed websites, unusable interfaces. Net art made from the web's own infrastructure rather than delivered through it.

key_works.title: wwwwwwwww.jodi.org
key_works.description: Website-as-artwork where the visible green ASCII revealed HTML source code as the actual piece.

key_works.title: OSS/***
key_works.description: Modified applications and games that expose how software constrains behavior.

entries.name: Olia Lialina
entries.medium: net art, web-based art, digital preservation
entries.summary: Made 'My Boyfriend Came Back from the War' in 1996 — hyperlinked narrative as emotional architecture. Became the movement's best historian, preserving GeoCities-era pages before anyone thought they mattered.

key_works.title: My Boyfriend Came Back from the War
key_works.description: HTML-frames narrative where the structure of the interface carries the emotional weight.

key_works.title: One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age
key_works.description: Archive and tumblr preserving GeoCities pages as a record of the vernacular web.

entries.name: Vuk Ćosić
entries.medium: net art, ASCII art, web-based art
entries.summary: Helped coin the term net.art. Understood early that the internet was a cultural medium, not a delivery channel. Shaped the movement's theoretical framework alongside its practice.

key_works.title: ASCII History of Moving Images
key_works.description: Classic films rendered in ASCII characters — a question about what survives translation between media.

entries.name: Heath Bunting
entries.medium: net art, activist art, systems art
entries.summary: Brought net art into activist territory — borders, identity systems, networked power. The political arm of the movement. Examines how networked systems encode control and movement.

key_works.title: The Status Project
key_works.description: Mapping the bureaucratic requirements for identity across borders.

entries.name: Cory Arcangel
entries.medium: hacked games, software art, video, prints
entries.summary: Hacked Super Mario, made paintings out of Photoshop gradients. Treats the tools of digital culture as art materials with deadpan precision. Examines the cultural weight packed into consumer software.

key_works.title: Super Mario Clouds
key_works.description: Modified NES cartridge showing only the clouds from Super Mario Bros — everything else removed.

key_works.title: Photoshop Gradient Demonstrations
key_works.description: Large-format paintings made using only the default Photoshop gradient tool.

entries.name: Jon Rafman
entries.medium: video, sculpture, digital photography, installation
entries.summary: Documents the emotional texture of being online — Google Street View as portraiture, deep-web aesthetics, strange beauty in overlooked corners of the network.

key_works.title: Nine Eyes of Google Street View
key_works.description: Curated collection of uncanny, poetic, and disturbing moments captured by Google's automated cameras.

entries.name: Petra Cortright
entries.medium: digital painting, webcam video, software-based art
entries.summary: Treated YouTube and the webcam as painting surfaces. Vernacular internet as fine-art material, without ironic distance. Her digital paintings collapse the line between screen-based and traditional media.

key_works.title: VVEBCAM
key_works.description: YouTube webcam video with keyword-tags as medium — later removed by YouTube, which became part of the piece.

entries.name: Amalia Ulman
entries.medium: performance, social media, video, installation
entries.summary: Performed 'Excellences & Perfections' on Instagram in 2014 — a scripted, months-long piece about class, femininity, and self-presentation on social media. One of the sharpest artworks about platform identity ever made.

key_works.title: Excellences & Perfections
key_works.description: Instagram performance with a fabricated life-story arc, scripted and staged to examine class aspiration on social platforms.

entries.name: Ed Atkins
entries.medium: CGI video, digital animation, installation
entries.summary: Makes CGI video about digital embodiment and the limits of rendered emotion. His avatars look nearly real and feel deeply wrong — which is the point.

key_works.title: Us Dead Talk Love
key_works.description: CGI video of a hyper-real digital figure reciting poetry about mortality and embodiment.

entries.name: Katja Novitskova
entries.medium: sculpture, installation, digital print on aluminum
entries.summary: Turned the internet's visual unconscious — stock imagery, scientific photography, algorithmic image selection — into physical sculptures. Materialises the logic of digital image circulation.

key_works.title: Post Internet Survival Guide
key_works.description: Publication and curatorial framework theorizing art after the internet became ambient.

key_works.title: Approximation series
key_works.description: Aluminium cutouts of viral and scientific images installed at human scale.

entries.name: Joshua Davis
entries.medium: generative software, creative coding, print
entries.summary: Was making generative art in Flash before most people knew the term. Pre-blockchain, pre-NFT — the OG of web-based generative practice, and a demonstration that code can produce emotionally resonant form.

key_works.title: Praystation
key_works.description: Flash-based generative art website that was one of the most visited art sites of the early web.

entries.name: Zach Lieberman
entries.medium: creative coding, interactive installation, openFrameworks
entries.summary: Co-created openFrameworks, taught at the School for Poetic Computation, and built a global creative-coding community through daily practice and radical openness. Artist, educator, and connective tissue for a whole field.

key_works.title: openFrameworks
key_works.description: Open-source C++ toolkit for creative coding, co-created with Theo Watson and Arturo Castro.

key_works.title: Daily Sketches
key_works.description: Publicly shared daily creative-coding practice — pedagogy disguised as practice.

entries.name: Tyler Hobbs
entries.medium: generative art, creative coding, on-chain art
entries.summary: Made Fidenza. Flowing, organic compositions with a recognisable algorithmic signature. Proved that generative systems could carry real emotional weight, not just geometric novelty. Fidenza became a landmark of the Art Blocks era.

key_works.title: Fidenza
key_works.description: 999 generative compositions using flow fields on Art Blocks — organic, painterly, algorithmically unique.

key_works.title: QQL
key_works.description: Collaborative generative project with Dandelion Wist exploring human-algorithm co-creation.

entries.name: Dmitri Cherniak
entries.medium: generative art, on-chain art, creative coding
entries.summary: Made Ringers — pegs and string, encoded in an algorithm, producing inexhaustible compositional variation. Simple rules generating expressive depth.

key_works.title: Ringers
key_works.description: 1000 generative compositions of pegs and wrapped string on Art Blocks — minimal rules, wide variation.

key_works.title: The Eternal Pump
key_works.description: Mechanical visualisation of perpetual motion rendered through generative code.

entries.name: Matt DesLauriers
entries.medium: generative art, creative coding, on-chain art
entries.summary: Pushes generative work toward the painterly — soft, textured, atmospheric. His output suggests code can reach the warmth people associate with handmade media.

key_works.title: Meridian
key_works.description: Generative landscapes with soft gradients and organic terrain on Art Blocks.

key_works.title: Subscapes
key_works.description: Generative seascapes exploring color, depth, and light in layered compositions.

entries.name: Robert Hodgin
entries.medium: generative art, particle systems, creative coding, simulation
entries.summary: Built particle systems and natural simulations that shaped what computational beauty looked like for a decade. Explores the aesthetic possibilities of physics, fluid dynamics, and emergent behaviour.

key_works.title: Magnetosphere
key_works.description: iTunes visualizer commission — particle system reacting to music, seen by millions.

key_works.title: Meander
key_works.description: Generative topographic landscapes on Art Blocks built from algorithmic river systems.

entries.name: Ben Fry
entries.medium: data visualization, creative coding, information design
entries.summary: Co-created Processing with Casey Reas. Built the infrastructure a generation of artists used to learn code as material. His own practice in data visualisation treats information as a site of aesthetic decision.

key_works.title: Processing
key_works.description: Open-source creative-coding language and IDE co-created with Casey Reas — the tool that put code in the hands of tens of thousands of artists.

key_works.title: Distellamap
key_works.description: Data-visualisation artwork mapping the structure of Atari 2600 game code.

entries.name: Golan Levin
entries.medium: creative coding, interactive installation, performance, openFrameworks
entries.summary: Built, taught, and curated a lineage of computational art at Carnegie Mellon's STUDIO for Creative Inquiry. His own work threads voice, gesture, and code into responsive instruments. Not named in the seed taxonomy article but central to the openFrameworks orbit the article discusses.

key_works.title: Messa di Voce
key_works.description: Interactive performance where vocal sounds are visualised in real time as coloured graphics.

entries.name: Kevin McCoy
entries.medium: video art, blockchain art, net art, NFTs
entries.summary: Minted Quantum in 2014 — the first NFT — and thereby opened the possibility of the entire category. Practice spans video, net art, and on-chain work, predating the crypto art market he helped make possible.

key_works.title: Quantum
key_works.description: The first NFT — a generative animation minted on Namecoin, predating the ERC-721 standard by years.

entries.name: Beeple
entries.medium: digital art, 3D rendering, NFTs
entries.summary: The $69 million Christie's sale forced the art market to confront digital art as a financial reality. His Everydays practice — a new piece every day for 5,000+ consecutive days — predates crypto and gives the position staying power beyond one auction.

key_works.title: Everydays: The First 5000 Days
key_works.description: Collage of 5,000 daily digital artworks sold at Christie's for $69.3 million.

key_works.title: HUMAN ONE
key_works.description: Kinetic sculpture — four video screens in a box displaying a figure walking through changing digital landscapes, updatable by the artist.

entries.name: XCOPY
entries.medium: glitch art, animated loops, crypto art
entries.summary: Defined the visual language of crypto art. Glitch, death loops, skeletal figures, memetic dread. The aesthetic DNA of the NFT movement runs through his work.

key_works.title: Right-click and Save As guy
key_works.description: Iconic glitch animation that became shorthand for crypto-art ownership debates.

key_works.title: A Coin for the Ferryman
key_works.description: Looping skeletal-figure death animation — a canonical crypto artwork.

entries.name: Mitchell Chan
entries.medium: smart contracts, conceptual art, blockchain art
entries.summary: Made 'Digital Zones of Immaterial Pictorial Sensibility' in 2017 — a direct reconstruction of Yves Klein's 1959 experiment as an Ethereum smart contract. One of the clearest bridges between postwar conceptual art and crypto-native practice.

key_works.title: Digital Zones of Immaterial Pictorial Sensibility
key_works.description: Ethereum smart contract mirroring Klein's immaterial zones — buyers exchange ETH for an invisible work, with the option to burn the token.

entries.name: Snowfro
entries.medium: generative art, platform design, on-chain art
entries.summary: Erick Calderon founded Art Blocks, the platform that made generative art collectible and verifiable on-chain. The platform is itself a creative act — infrastructure that enabled a whole movement. Also the artist behind Chromie Squiggle.

key_works.title: Chromie Squiggle
key_works.description: Art Blocks genesis project — generative squiggles that became the platform's signature.

entries.name: Matt Kane
entries.medium: generative art, blockchain-responsive art, digital painting
entries.summary: Made 'Right Place & Right Time,' a painting whose colors shift dynamically based on Bitcoin's price. One of the first works to treat on-chain data as a live artistic input rather than a sales mechanism.

key_works.title: Right Place & Right Time
key_works.description: Digital painting that changes colors based on Bitcoin's price — blockchain data as live material.

entries.name: Sarah Zucker
entries.medium: hand-drawn animation, VHS art, crypto art, mixed media
entries.summary: Works across analog and digital — hand-drawn animation, VHS texture, crypto distribution. Evidence that blockchain art doesn't have to look like blockchain.

key_works.title: All Dimensions
key_works.description: VHS-textured animations combining hand-drawn elements with analog video processing, distributed via blockchain.

entries.name: Kim Asendorf
entries.medium: pixel sorting, glitch art, generative art, creative coding
entries.summary: Invented pixel sorting — the technique that became the default glitch aesthetic across digital and crypto art. SABOTAGE and later series keep pushing algorithmic image manipulation forward.

key_works.title: Pixel Sorting
key_works.description: Invented the pixel-sorting technique — algorithmically rearranging pixels by brightness or hue, spawning a visual movement.

key_works.title: SABOTAGE
key_works.description: Series of algorithmic image manipulations extending pixel sorting and glitch aesthetics.

entries.name: Hackatao
entries.medium: digital art, mixed media, crypto art, mythological illustration
entries.summary: Duo of Sergio Scalet and Nadia Squarci. Built a consistent mythological visual world across years of practice — one of the few crypto artists constructing a universe rather than releasing drops.

key_works.title: Queens+Kings
key_works.description: Series of mythological portrait NFTs building a coherent imagined world.

entries.name: Robbie Barrat
entries.medium: GAN art, neural networks, AI art
entries.summary: Trained GANs on Old Master paintings as a teenager. His AI-generated nudes and landscapes are now considered early canonical works of AI art. Young enough and early enough to hold a permanent position in the medium's short history.

key_works.title: AI Generated Nude Portrait #1
key_works.description: GAN trained on classical nude paintings producing uncanny, melting figure compositions — sold at auction before the AI art boom.

entries.name: Trevor Paglen
entries.medium: photography, installation, AI, machine vision
entries.summary: Uses AI to interrogate surveillance, classification, and machine vision. Not decorative — political. His work reveals what AI does to the world, not what it makes for us. MacArthur Fellow.

key_works.title: ImageNet Roulette
key_works.description: Web application exposing biased and offensive classifications in the ImageNet training dataset.

key_works.title: Orbital Reflector
key_works.description: Satellite sculpture launched into orbit — a non-functional object questioning militarisation of space.

entries.name: Jesse Kanda
entries.medium: video, visual direction, digital art
entries.summary: Visual collaborator for Arca, FKA twigs, Björk. Co-defined a visual-sonic language where uncanny bodies and machine-textured skin become primary material. Named in the seed taxonomy article as a pivotal collaborator.

key_works.title: Mutant
key_works.description: Music video for Arca — rubbery, translucent figures as embodied sound.

entries.name: Rafael Lozano-Hemmer
entries.medium: interactive installation, biometric art, public art
entries.summary: Builds interactive public installations using biometrics, surveillance technology, and crowd participation. The visitor's body becomes both subject and material at architectural scale.

key_works.title: Pulse Room
key_works.description: Installation of 300 incandescent bulbs flickering to the heartbeats of participants.

key_works.title: Vectorial Elevation
key_works.description: Robotic searchlights controlled remotely via the internet — public art at city scale.

entries.name: Random International
entries.medium: installation, responsive environments, kinetic sculpture
entries.summary: Hannes Koch and Florian Ortkrass. Made Rain Room — a field of falling water that pauses wherever a body moves. Technology that responds to human presence, rendered as weather.

key_works.title: Rain Room
key_works.description: 100-square-metre field of falling water that pauses wherever a body is detected — exhibited at MoMA, Barbican, and globally.

entries.name: Arca
entries.medium: electronic music, visual collaboration, production, performance
entries.summary: Alejandra Ghersi. Producer and artist whose visual collaboration with Jesse Kanda redefined what a pop-adjacent audiovisual practice could be. Collaborator with Björk, Kanye West, FKA twigs.

key_works.title: KICK i-v
key_works.description: Five-album cycle building a self-mythological world across production, imagery, and performance.

entries.name: Lawrence Lek
entries.medium: CGI, game engine, film, installation
entries.summary: Builds CGI worlds that extend into film, game, and installation — speculative fictions about AI sentience, labor, and Sinofuturism rendered through game-engine aesthetics.

key_works.title: Sinofuturism
key_works.description: Video essay reframing 'Sinofuturism' as a category of analysis for AI, labour, and copying as production.

key_works.title: Black Cloud
key_works.description: CGI film following a sentient self-driving car through a post-human city.

entries.name: Sondra Perry
entries.medium: video, installation, web-based art
entries.summary: Works across video, installation, and the browser. Examines the racialised texture of digital infrastructure — the blue of the rotoscope, the default skin of avatar systems.

key_works.title: Typhoon coming on
key_works.description: Installation using rotoscoped CGI and Turner's slave-ship painting to trace the circulation of Black bodies in digital and historical space.

entries.name: Nicolas Jaar
entries.medium: electronic music, sound installation, radio
entries.summary: Producer and composer whose work sits between electronic music and sound art. Founded Other People, ran the long-form web experience 'The Network,' collapsed the distance between album, installation, and broadcast.

key_works.title: Space Is Only Noise
key_works.description: Debut album framing electronic composition as an ambient architecture of sound and silence.

entries.name: Rhea Myers
entries.medium: conceptual art, smart contracts, writing
entries.summary: Early conceptual artist working with code, blockchains, and ownership as medium. Writes, builds, critiques. Her smart-contract works pre-date the NFT boom and reach back into 2010s conceptual practice.

key_works.title: Is Art
key_works.description: Smart contract that toggles whether the contract 'is art,' with every state change recorded on-chain.

entries.name: Simon Denny
entries.medium: installation, sculpture, crypto art
entries.summary: Makes installations that parse the material culture of tech industries — Bitcoin mining, corporate presentation aesthetics, platform capitalism rendered as sculpture.

key_works.title: Proof of Work
key_works.description: Exhibition examining the material and ideological infrastructure of Bitcoin mining.

entries.name: Addie Wagenknecht
entries.medium: sculpture, painting, installation, feminist tech
entries.summary: Works at the intersection of feminist theory, surveillance, and automated painting. Cofounded F.A.T. Lab. Uses drones and machine learning to make work that questions authorship and domestic labour.

key_works.title: Asymmetric Love
key_works.description: Sculpture of an ornamental chandelier made entirely of black surveillance cameras.

entries.name: Lynn Hershman Leeson
entries.medium: net art, film, installation, AI
entries.summary: Pioneer of net-adjacent practice decades before the net. Her 'Agent Ruby' (1999-2002) was an early AI chatbot exhibited as art; her decades of work have tracked identity, biotech, and surveillance before those became canonical subjects.

key_works.title: Agent Ruby
key_works.description: Early AI chatbot presented as a fictional character and exhibited at SFMOMA.

key_works.title: Roberta Breitmore
key_works.description: Long-running performance of a fictional woman whose identity was documented bureaucratically — a precursor to online persona art.

entries.name: Primavera De Filippi
entries.medium: smart contracts, legal theory, DAO art, research
entries.summary: Artist-researcher whose 'Plantoid' project demonstrated a self-owning, self-reproducing plant-bot powered by Ethereum — one of the clearest art-objects of DAO logic. Also a core legal theorist of blockchain governance.

key_works.title: Plantoid
key_works.description: Robotic plant that pays artists to produce new Plantoids using funds it receives on-chain — a self-reproducing DAO artwork.
